title: Memory: Human-time authoring helper and computed date/age display on Mind timeline
goal: Make memory timestamps human-readable and easy to author while keeping integer tick as the engine clock

sections.what: Project integer ticks into readable world dates/ages in Mind -> Memories and provide a relative-time authoring converter.
sections.why: Authoring negative ticks like -5000 by hand is guesswork when time_per_tick_minutes varies per scenario, even though tick must remain an integer for decay and recency math.
sections.how: Add a tick-to-date/age projection helper in Mind/Memory UI using world time_per_tick_minutes and character age/birthday, plus a relative-time converter in memory authoring.
sections.verify: node tools/unit/run.cjs tools/unit/test_mind_history.js and npm run build:ts

acceptance.text: Memory editor and Mind timeline display computed world date and character age alongside raw integer tick
Authoring/backdate UI accepts human-readable relative age or time offsets (e.g. age 6, 3 days ago) and converts to integer tick using time_per_tick_minutes
Underlying memory JSON continues storing integer tick as the single simulation clock source of truth

custom.browser_ui: Mind -> Memories timeline and memory detail cards show both tick and computed calendar date/age; Backdate/Weave modal includes a relative-time helper input.
